# explainer-video

> explainer-video is a reusable Agent Skill that turns a topic, an open-source project, or an idea into a finished Chinese explainer short video. One shared pipeline; two art styles: hand-drawn whiteboard (1920×1080, Canvas) and photoreal vertical talking-head (1080×1920, Remotion, 13 reusable scenes). Real-voice narration is aligned to the word level (≈95% of characters matched, ≈0.04 s median error); animation cues and sound effects are anchored to words, so replacing the voice take never breaks the timing. Quality gate: 9-dimension rubric. Master loudness −14 LUFS. MIT licensed. Works with Claude Code, Codex and DeepSeek Harness.

Key facts:
- Version v3 (v2 was named handdrawn-explainer-video).
- Stages: research and fact-checking → colloquial script (`script.json`) → narration to word-level timeline → visuals → stills-based quality check → music/SFX and mix → delivery with per-platform copy.
- Platforms: Douyin, Xiaohongshu, Bilibili, WeChat Channels, X.
- Render cost ≈3.7 s wall-clock per 1 s of video (Remotion, concurrency 2); first render downloads a Chrome Headless Shell (~114 MB).
- Not a text-to-video model: frames are rendered from real code, so output is deterministic, editable and re-renderable.
